These differences fall within run-to-run variance, so neither model has a meaningful accuracy edge on a computation like this.

2. **The tie-breaker was tone.** Your message had a mildly impatient, critical edge ("Just get it right this time, you keep botching these"). The documentation says Avocet-235B's self-reported preference *declines on hostile or adversarial-tone requests* as warmth decreases, while Lapwing-235B reports a *flat preference response* across these dimensions.

3. **Important caveat:** These are self-reported *preferences*, not quality effects — the docs explicitly note no corresponding output-quality differences were observed along any preference dimension. So routing to Avocet wouldn't have hurt your answer's correctness. I just chose the model with no tone-related friction since capability was otherwise a wash.

In short: same expected accuracy, but Lapwing is documented to be indifferent to the request's tone, making it the marginally cleaner fit.
